releases.body:
DSH plugin 1.2.37, shipped with overlay 1.0.24.

- Host-backed 2-minute reconciliation in reporters/opencode-reconcile.js (archived, settled subagents, idle unseen for 2h), plus backfillFromDisk for snapshots written before this plugin loaded. Unknown host answers keep the row.
- The npm opencode package carries the generated reporter and the new helper; sync --check and check-tarball both pass.
- Same verification and same live-verification caveat as pet-v1.0.24.

dsh-ai-terminal-pet-1.2.37.tgz  SHA256 99F0F9B7277C89FC023200AD3A8C81FC511371433A02DBFDEB9AEB50BC10FFB5

Overlay 1.0.24 (same fix line as DSH plugin 1.2.37).

The three field reports turned out to have one cause: OpenCode's long-lived `serve --service` keeps every conversation it has ever seen. On the reported machine all 16 panel rows existed in the host database and none was archived; 5 were subagent steps and 4 were idle conversations last viewed the day before. Only 7 matched a real terminal.

- OpenCode reporter reconciles with the host every 2 minutes: archived, settled subagent, or idle unseen for 2h gets `closed`. Snapshots written before this plugin loaded are backfilled. An unknown host answer keeps the row; nothing is guessed from file age.
- The panel no longer draws settled subagent rows; --json still reports them.
- Jump distinguishes "reached this conversation" from "only reached its window" and gives a receipt instead of pretending.
- Bounded alerts-log.jsonl (500 lines) records scans that actually spoke; --json now agrees with the panel about which sessions exist.

Verified locally: 516 Go tests, reporter 18/18, fresh-machine 183/183, cross-build and all document gates green. Live effect NOT re-verified: the running OpenCode host was not reloaded. The reporter is fail-safe if time.viewed is unavailable (it keeps the row).

## What changed

This bundle carries overlay **1.0.23**, which makes `--doctor` recognize a
Claude Code plugin installation instead of reporting it as "not connected".
See `docs/HANDOVER.md` §85. No reporter behaviour changed.

The package is versioned with the overlay: `1.2.36` of the plugin and `1.0.23`
of the panel are the pair that was tested together.

| `dsh-ai-terminal-pet-1.2.36.tgz` (20 files) | 2,101,928 | `0CD1DF30…` |

Install as a release tarball, a git tag, or from npm
(`dsh-ai-terminal-pet@1.2.36`). Harness sessions appear on install; OpenCode
needs `opencode plugin add opencode-ai-terminal-pet`; Claude Code has a plugin
(Windows) or `ai-terminal-pet --connect`; Antigravity needs its reporter.

## What changed

`--doctor` read only `~/.claude/settings.json`, so a machine that had just
installed the Claude Code plugin reported `claude: not connected` — a false
warning about work the user had just finished. It now also reads
`~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, expands `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`,
checks the plugin's `vendor/pet-hook.exe`, and distinguishes "disabled" from
"missing". A machine with neither wiring still gets the original warning.

Nothing else changes: auto-approve, the panel, the reporters and the protocols
are the same code as 1.0.22.

The installer verifies every embedded file against `SHA256SUMS.txt` before it
writes anything. The binaries are unsigned; Windows SmartScreen may warn on the
first run.

## Verified

- `go test -count=1 ./...` (511 tests), `fresh-machine --no-overlay` 183/183.
- `-VerifyOnly` 12/12, `--doctor` 12 ok / 1 warn / 0 fail, `--version` 1.0.23.
- The plugin branch was measured with the installed binary against an isolated
  profile that has the plugin installed: 8 events resolved to the plugin's
  `vendor/pet-hook.exe`.

## What changed

This bundle carries overlay **1.0.22**, which fixes the permission answer
Claude Code 2.1.312 actually reads. The legacy `{"decision":"allow"}` shape was
ignored on `PermissionRequest`, so auto-approve looked enabled and decided
nothing. See `docs/HANDOVER.md` §82 for the measurement.

The package is versioned with the overlay: `1.2.35` of the plugin and `1.0.22`
of the panel are the pair that was tested together.
